about: GPUs: why AI made Nvidia rich. Factory #12, backlog row 13. Number hook, then a true story, then one mechanism. Nvidia's quarter ended July 26, 2026: revenue $96.2 billion, Data Center $89.0 billion (about 92.5%) (Nvidia earnings release, Aug 26, 2026). Its chips started out in games: in fiscal 2016 Gaming was $2,818M of $5,010M and Datacenter $339M (Nvidia FY2017 10-K). In 2012 Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton (University of Toronto) trained AlexNet on two GTX 580 3GB GPUs in five to six days and won ILSVRC-2012 with 15.3% top-5 error vs 26.2% for the second-best entry (NeurIPS 2012 paper); the GTX 580 was a $499, 512-core GeForce card launched in 2010 for DX11 games (Nvidia launch release and datasheet). Neural-network layers are matrix multiplications, each made of fused multiply-adds (Nvidia Deep Learning Performance docs, GEMM guide): one 4,096 x 4,096 x 4,096 product is about 69 billion multiply-adds (our arithmetic). A MacBook Air (M5) has a 10-core CPU (Apple specs); a GeForce RTX 5090 has 21,760 CUDA cores (Nvidia specs), small simple cores, not the same kind. Nvidia's own explainer: GPUs are ideal for graphics, where the work 'has to be done at once'. Hero moment: line 'once', one print-block slam fills the whole multiply-add sheet. No stock price, no investment advice. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.
